bihar_raw_news.title: Guwahati Spy Scare: Assam STF Arrests Bihar Man Over Alleged Pakistan Intelligence Connection
bihar_raw_news.content: News Development Guwahati Spy Scare: Assam STF Arrests Bihar Man Over Alleged Pakistan Intelligence Connection By Hub Network October 4, 2026 0 244 Share Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Must read White Coats Turn Saffron: 73 Private-Sector Doctors Join BJP in Assam October 4, 2026 Shillong airport expansion on track, international airport vision in blueprint: Sniawbhalang Dhar October 4, 2026 Hapoh 2 snem la lah ban hiar liengsuin ba heh ha Shillong airport : Sniawbha October 4, 2026 Kyrpad u Chairman ka GCCM ia u MP ban pan na ka bynta ka kaiphod NSCT ha Parliament October 4, 2026 Hub Network Guwahati, Oct 4: The Assam Police Special Task Force (STF) on Sunday apprehended a 31-year-old man from Bihar in Guwahati for his alleged association with a Pakistan Intelligence Operative (PIO), which investigators suspect could be linked to an espionage network operating in Assam. The accused, Abhishek Kumar Singh, a resident of Bihar’s Purba Champaran district, was held from a rented accommodation in Gandhinagar under Satgaon Police Station during a search operation conducted by the Assam STF on Sunday. According to Assam STF sources, Singh was allegedly working as an informer for the Pakistan Intelligence Operative and sharing information related to security forces. The operation was launched on the basis of intelligence inputs provided by Gajraj MI, Tezpur, officials said. “The operation was launched on the basis of preliminary information received from Gajraj MI, Tezpur,” the police said. Following the intelligence input, STF IG Partha Sarathi Mahanta, working in close coordination with Sonitpur SSP Barun Purkayastha, developed further information about Singh and his alleged involvement and links with a Pakistan Intelligence Operative. The STF subsequently carried out an operation in Guwahati and apprehended Singh from his rented house. During the operation, police seized a mobile phone, SIM cards and documents, which investigators described as incriminating. According to the Assam Police, preliminary investigation has indicated Singh’s alleged involvement in espionage activities, including sharing confidential information concerning security forces with the Pakistan Intelligence Operative. The arrest followed a joint intelligence-development exercise by Military Intelligence and the Assam Police STF. Investigators are now probing the extent of the alleged network and the nature of the information that may have been shared. Further investigation is underway. bihar_raw_news.title: School roof in Bihar's Kiratpur held up by benches, bricks after pillar collapses | India News
bihar_raw_news.content: A government primary school in Bihar ’s Darbhanga district has been left with a makeshift support system after a pillar of its ageing building collapsed, with benches, desks, and bricks being used to support a portion of the roof. The school building, constructed in 1983 under the Centre’s "Operation Blackboard" programme, has developed several structural problems (Sourced) The precarious structure at Kiratpur Primary School in Alinagar block has raised concerns about the safety of the 191 children enrolled there. Although classes are not currently held beneath the portion supported by the makeshift arrangement, students and teachers continue to pass through the area. The school building, constructed in 1983 under the Centre’s "Operation Blackboard" programme, has developed several structural problems. The roof leaks during rain, while beams and pillars are in a dilapidated condition. Plaster has fallen off in several places, and reinforcement bars have become exposed. After one of the pillars collapsed some three to four months ago, benches, desks and bricks were placed underneath the roof instead of constructing a replacement pillar, according to school authorities. Read More Also read: Delhi amends school rules, makes essentiality certificate mandatory for schools seeking institutional land What teachers and villagers say Assistant teacher Pawan Kumar Choudhary said the education department and other officials had been informed several times about the condition of the building. Villagers have also staged protests seeking a solution. “After the pillar collapsed, benches and desks were used to support the roof. The danger remains,” he said. Villager Parjit Yadav said repeated appeals had been made regarding the safety of the children. “If a new building is not constructed soon, we will launch an agitation,” he said. Headmaster Rajendra Kumar said the school had informed officials from the block to the district level around five to six times. Written communications were also sent, and officials had inspected the school, but no permanent repairs or replacement building had been provided so far. The official stance When contacted on Saturday, Darbhanga district education officer (DEO) Vidyanand Thakur said steps had already been taken for the construction of a new building. He said the old building had been declared unsafe and that no teaching activities were being conducted there. “The existing two-room building was constructed as the first primary school in this village in 1983 under Operation Blackboard. At present, teaching is being conducted in the kitchen shed on the school premises,” Thakur said. According to the DEO, the existing building has limited usable space, with an almirah occupying one room and benches and desks kept in another room and in the verandah. He said an estimate for the construction of a new building had already been submitted to the department. He said a new six-room school building had been proposed and would be constructed by the Bihar School Infrastructure Development Corporation. national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 131 PM-SETU completes one year, aims to modernise Government ITIs
national_raw_news.content: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) has completed one year today. The PM-SETU scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was launched on 4th of October last year. The initiative seeks to strengthen industry-led governance, upgrade training infrastructure and promote demand-driven courses in line with evolving workforce requirements. It aims to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training by transforming Government India’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into modern, industry-aligned training institutions. The scheme has a total outlay of over 60 thousand crore rupees, comprising 30 thousand crore rupees from the Centre, 20 thousand crore rupees from States and 10 thousand crore rupees from industry. ITIs provide vocational training to equip youth with practical skills for employment and industry. Under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), training is offered through Government and Private Industrial Training Institutes in engineering and non-engineering trades. Its course duration varies from six months to two years, depending on the trade. The Directorate General of Training is the apex organisation responsible for the development and coordination of vocational training at the national level. The total number of ITIs, including Government and Private, in the country has increased to over 13 thousand in 2026 from over nine thousand in 2014, indicating an increase of 42 percent. Further, enrolment in ITIs across the country has also increased to 14.70 lakh in the academic session 2025-26 from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014-15, indicating an increase of 54 percent. At the national level, the Ministry has constituted a National Steering Committee (NSC) to provide overall direction for the scheme. Since its implementation, 850 ITIs have been identified, comprising 172 Hub ITIs and 678 Spoke ITIs. The NSC has also approved the transition of PM-SETU from its pilot phase to a nationwide rollout across all 200 identified ITI clusters. The rollout enables States and Union Territories to take up implementation based on industry readiness and implementation capacity. Approval has been given to Strategic Investment Plans for 14 ITI clusters under PM-SETU with an investment of over 3 thousand 446 crore rupees.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | International 280 Saudi Arabia rejects Houthi claim of attack on Riyadh; Yemeni forces say they neutralised hundred...
national_raw_news.content: Saudi Arabia has rejected a Houthi claim that Riyadh was targeted in a missile and drone attack, while Yemeni forces reported heavy losses among Houthi fighters on key fronts in Yemen. Coalition Spokesman of Saudi-led coalition Yemen, Major General Turki Al Malki has rejected the Houthi claim that Riyadh had been targeted, describing it as misleading. The Spokesman has been quoted by Saudi Arabia’s media saying that the Houthis were seeking to project an “illusory victory” amid losses suffered in Taiz – a key front in Yemen. He added that the Houthis are seeking to divert attention from the huge losses that they are suffering. Earlier, Houthi-affiliated channel – Al Masirah, had reported Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Sare’e saying that they had launched a ballistic missile and drone operation targeting Aramco in Riyadh. Sare’e claimed the strikes hit their targets and caused fires, saying the attack was in response to Saudi airstrikes and missile attacks on Sana’a and other Yemeni provinces. Meanwhile, Saba News Agency in Aden reported that Yemeni armed forces of the internationally recognised government carried out 97 operations against Houthi reinforcements on the Tur al-Bahah and Taiz fronts. It said the operations killed or neutralised 260 Houthi fighters and destroyed or disabled 44 military vehicles and transport and supply assets. The forces have also reportedly struck Houthi targets in Sana’a and Saada, as fighting continues to intensify across the conflict’s important fronts.

national_raw_news.title: Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma Highlights Lord Mahavira’s Teachings for Peaceful Society 1 hour ago 26
national_raw_news.content: Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma called for forgiveness, non-violence, and universal friendship while highlighting the teachings of Lord Mahavira. Speaking at the Collective Forgiveness, World Friendship Day and Jain Ratna Felicitation Ceremony in Ghatkopar, Mumbai, the Governor said that Jain principles such as truth, non-violence, non-stealing, non-possession and celibacy can help build a peaceful and humane society. He emphasized that forgiveness and friendship should go beyond religious and social boundaries. The Governor also highlighted the Jain philosophy of Anekantavada, which teaches respect for different perspectives and encourages dialogue to resolve conflicts. He described forgiveness as a sign of inner strength and said that Jainism’s compassion extends to all living beings. He also recalled the influence of Jain principles of non-violence on Mahatma Gandhi through his spiritual mentor, Shrimad Rajchandraji. Governor Varma praised the 126-year-old Bharat Jain Mahamandal for its contribution to spiritual values, social unity and humanitarian service. Skill Development Minister Mangalprabhat Lodha urged the Jain community to participate in government welfare and cleanliness initiatives and to support people, farmers and livestock during droughts. During the event, Governor Varma presented Jain Ratna Awards to MLA Parag Shah, Sukharaj Nahar, Kailashchand Jain and Suresh Goyal for their contributions to society. The ceremony was attended by several public representatives, Jain saints, monks, nuns and members of the Bharat Jain Mahamandal.
